title: Etale descent of finite functorial log blowup procedures
statement: Consider quasi-compact locally Noetherian fs log schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with torsion-free characteristic group completions. Suppose a rule $\mathcal T$ is given on the members admitting a global fan chart [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup]. It assigns a finite ordered tower of saturated log blowups with nonempty coherent log ideal centers. Assume that the assignment is independent of the chosen fan chart, and for every strict etale morphism between these members its source tower is canonically the contracted pullback of its target tower. Here pullback recursively blows up pulled-back ideals and contraction deletes only centers equal to the whole log monoid sheaf. Assume that these comparisons preserve centers and order, respect identities and composition, and that the rule is defined also on finite disjoint unions with the same compatibilities for the component inclusions. Then $\mathcal T$ extends, uniquely up to the canonical isomorphisms of contracted towers with centers, to all the indicated fs log schemes, with the same strict etale pullback compatibility. The extension is a finite saturated log blowup tower, and its centers are nonempty coherent ideals. Its contracted pullback to each chart neighborhood is the prescribed tower there.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, pp.109--110, initial descent reduction and final finite-disjoint-union argument; effective gluing input implicit there, using 3.3.8--3.3.10 for log blowups.

proof.text: First note that every assigned tower is contracted. Apply the assumed comparison to the identity of a charted log scheme: a finite ordered tower is isomorphic, with its centers, to its own contraction only if no stage was deleted. Whole-monoid centers give identity morphisms, since their pullbacks are generated by the unit under every fs log morphism, so the identity has the defining blowup universal property. Only whole-monoid centers are deleted: a proper principal ideal is retained even though its blowup is an isomorphism. On the empty scheme every ideal sheaf is the whole monoid sheaf, so the assigned contracted tower has length zero. Define the extension on the empty scheme to be this tower.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.10, contraction and universal properties; identity comparison hypothesis

proof.text: For nonempty $(X,M)$ choose the finite strict etale chart cover $u_a:U_a\to X$ supplied by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](i). Put $U=\coprod_a U_a$, with log structure and chart obtained componentwise, and $u:U\to X$. The coproduct lemma supplies disjoint open-and-closed components; its finite-coproduct consequence gives quasi-compactness. A disjoint union of the target fans, with its componentwise monoid sheaf, is a fine fan by the local definition, and the componentwise characteristic isomorphisms make $U$ globally fan-charted. The log scheme is locally Noetherian because its components are, and its characteristic stalks are their stalks. The map $u$ is strict, surjective and etale: on each disjoint open component it is $u_a$, and the affine-local definition of etaleness is exactly the definition there. Thus the given rule, including its finite-union compatibility, supplies one finite contracted tower $S=\mathcal T(U)$ of length $n$, with ordered centers $J_i\subset M_{U_i}$ for $0\leq i<n$. We use this single tower, not separate orderings of the component towers.

source.place: VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed pp.109--110; descent details expanded

proof.text: The overlap $R=U\times_XU$ and the triple overlap are legitimate inputs for the rule. Indeed $X$ is quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian lemma. Since $U$ is quasi-compact, $u$ is quasi-compact by the permanence lemma; its base changes and their sources over a quasi-compact base are quasi-compact by that same lemma. Apply this successively for double and triple overlaps. Their projections are strict etale and surjective by etale-cover base change. They are locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], since etale morphisms are locally of finite type. The strict pullback assertion of the fan-chart lemma supplies global fan charts from $U$, and strictness identifies their characteristic stalks with those upstairs on $U$. Thus these overlaps are fs with torsion-free characteristic groups. The same reasoning applies to common refinements of any two such finite chart covers, and to $Y\times_XU$ when $Y\to X$ is strict etale with $Y$ in the indicated class.

source.place: Tags 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence), 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change); properties.tex Tag 01OY; morphisms.tex Tags 01T6, 02GO, 01S1; ILO VIII 3.3.12--3.3.13

proof.text: Here is the stagewise cover check used below. Pull a finite log blowup tower back along a surjective strict etale map $A\to B$. The log-ideal construction commutes with strict etale restriction, so at each stage $A_i\to B_i$ is the scheme-theoretic base change of $A\to B$ and is again a surjective strict etale cover. For an ideal $I_i\subset M_{B_i}$, its restriction is the whole monoid sheaf if and only if $I_i=M_{B_i}$: if the restriction is whole, every local section of $M_{B_i}$ belongs to $I_i$ after the cover, and the sheaf condition for the subsheaf $I_i$ glues its local representatives. The reverse implication is immediate. Consequently a surjective strict etale pullback deletes no stages of a contracted tower. This argument needs no surjectivity of the blowup morphisms themselves.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.10; sites.tex Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets); morphisms.tex Tags 02GO and 01S1

proof.text: Apply the assumed comparisons to both projections $p_1,p_2:R\to U$. By Step 4 neither pullback of $S$ loses a stage, so both are uncontracted towers of length $n$, canonically identified with $\mathcal T(R)$. Composing one identification with the inverse of the other gives an isomorphism $p_1^*S\simeq p_2^*S$ of ordered towers with centers over $R$. In particular corresponding centers, on the identified levels, are equal as subideals of the same log structure. On triple overlaps the two composite identifications equal the direct one: all three are the comparisons with $\mathcal T(U\times_XU\times_XU)$ prescribed by the composition hypothesis. The diagonal comparison is the identity by the identity hypothesis. This gives a descent datum for every stage, including its actual ideal, with one common index set $0,\ldots,n-1$.

source.place: VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed pp.109--110; descent details expanded

proof.text: We descend the centers inductively, retaining this index set. Suppose that $X_i$ has been constructed and that $U_i\simeq U\times_XX_i$, with the overlap identifications of Step 5 identifying $R_i$ with $U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$; initially this is $X_0=X$. Strictness identifies $M_{U_i}$ with the restriction of $M_i$ on the localized etale site. The equalities of centers on $R_i$ therefore make the sheaf $J_i$ into a sheaf descent datum on the covering $U_i\to X_i$. Use the small-site and universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], with all covering objects and the displayed finite fiber products in its chosen universe. The set-sheaf cover-descent lemma glues it to a sheaf $I_i$ and glues its inclusions into $M_i$. This map is injective: sections with the same image agree after the cover because each local inclusion is injective, and hence agree by the sheaf condition. Identify $I_i$ with its image in $M_i$. Explicitly, for etale $W\to X_i$, its sections are precisely the $m\in M_i(W)$ whose restrictions to $W\times_{X_i}U_i$ belong to $J_i$. This also proves uniqueness as a subobject. Stability under multiplication by $M_i$ is checked after this cover and follows from ideal stability for $J_i$. Nonemptiness and coherence hold because the same etale-local finite nonempty monoid generators that define $J_i$ define the restriction of $I_i$; these are local conditions in the definition of a coherent log ideal.

source.place: Tags 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps); ILO VIII 3.3.7 for coherent log ideals

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] to $(X_i,M_i)$ and $I_i$ to obtain the saturated log blowup $(X_{i+1},M_{i+1})$. Its hypotheses are exactly local Noetherianity, fs and a nonempty coherent log ideal, as established at the initial stage and Step 6; the output is again an fs log scheme in the locally-Noetherian convention of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Strict etale restriction of this construction identifies its pullback on $U_i$ with the specified blowup along $J_i$, by the universal property. Hence $U_{i+1}\simeq U\times_XX_{i+1}$, and the identical assertion on double overlaps identifies the descended transition with the transition of Step 5. The cover-base-change lemma shows that $U_{i+1}\to X_{i+1}$ is a surjective etale cover. This completes the inductive step, so induction for $i=0,\ldots,n-1$ constructs the entire global tower. Each center $I_i$ is proper: if it were whole, its restriction $J_i$ would be whole, contrary to Step 1. Thus the tower is contracted and finite of length exactly $n$, and its uncontracted pullback to $U$ is $S$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10, global chart construction and strict etale compatibility

proof.text: The construction is independent of the chosen finite chart cover. For two covers $U\to X$ and $V\to X$, the common refinement $W=U\times_XV$ has a global fan chart and is quasi-compact by Step 3. Both projections are surjective strict etale. Their comparisons identify $\mathcal T(W)$ with the full pullbacks of $\mathcal T(U)$ and $\mathcal T(V)$, without deleting stages by Step 4; in particular the two lengths agree. At stage zero the two descended centers agree because their restrictions to the common cover $W$ agree, by the sectionwise description of Step 6. Their universal blowups are therefore uniquely isomorphic over $X$. Repeating this at successive stages gives the canonical comparison of the entire towers with centers. The same argument proves its uniqueness and its cocycle identity on three choices: the centers are equal after their common covering and each blowup has a unique isomorphism over the preceding stage. Chart choices introduce no further choice because the prescribed rule is chart independent.

source.place: VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed pp.109--110; descent details expanded

proof.text: Let $f:(Y,N)\to(X,M)$ be strict etale between members of the indicated class, and let $U\to X$ be the cover above. The scheme $W=Y\times_XU$ is quasi-compact, locally Noetherian and globally fan-charted by Step 3, and $W\to Y$ is a surjective strict etale cover. On $W$ the pulled-back global tower is the pullback of $\mathcal T(U)$; its contraction is $\mathcal T(W)$ by the assumed comparison for $W\to U$. At every stage, a center on the tower over $Y$ is whole if and only if its restriction to the covering stage over $W$ is whole, by Step 4. Thus contraction over $Y$ deletes exactly the indices deleted over $W$, even if several consecutive indices are deleted. After a deleted index the transition is canonically the identity by Step 1, so subsequent centers correspond unchanged. The surviving centers descend from exactly those of $\mathcal T(W)$. Step 6 and the blowup universal property then identify the contracted pullback over $Y$ with the extension constructed using the single chart cover $W\to Y$. By Step 8 that is the extension on $Y$. These comparisons preserve centers and order. Their identity and composition laws hold after a chart cover by the original laws for the rule, and hence globally by uniqueness of the descended ideals and of their universal blowups.

source.place: VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed pp.109--110; descent details expanded

proof.text: If $X$ itself has a global fan chart, use the identity as its cover in the construction: all centers descend to themselves, and the result is canonically $\mathcal T(X)$. Step 9 consequently gives the prescribed contracted tower on every chart neighborhood of any $X$. Finally consider any extension with the asserted compatibilities. Contract its whole-monoid stages, which are identities by Step 1. Its pullback to the finite surjective chart cover $U\to X$ has no further deletions by Step 4, and is $\mathcal T(U)$. Its first center must be the unique subideal descending $J_0$ by the sectionwise formula of Step 6. The first blowup is then the universal one, uniquely isomorphic over $X$ to ours. Induction gives the same assertion at every remaining stage. Thus the two contracted towers, together with their centers, are canonically isomorphic, and these isomorphisms respect all strict etale comparisons by the same uniqueness. This proves the required uniqueness and completes the extension.
